scores.evidence: Inline call on production traffic | V2 (falls back safely), V5 (latency at load)
scores.rationale: An explicit dependency map and gates (V1→mirror, V3→schema, V4→training, V2/V5→inline, V6/V7→enforcement) order phases from substrate upward.

scores.evidence: A real authorization on an issuer test-BIN card ... goes through the production auth host. The auth host calls the decision service
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real end-to-end production slice, with deploy, rollback and trace, before any features.

scores.evidence: Failure behavior (fail open vs closed) | R3 ... Default: Fall back to the current decision ... Flip condition: V2 fails
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions are listed with reversibility, default, assumption, validation and flip conditions, and unknowns are labelled.

scores.evidence: Phase 1: Contracts, privacy boundary and fail-safe guardrails ... Phase 5: Randomized enforcement on 1%, then 5%, 25% and 100% of one portfolio
scores.rationale: Widest-impact items (contracts, privacy boundary, fail-safes, schema identifiers) come before leaf work, and exposure widens in stages.

scores.evidence: Test BINs only; tokenized PAN; mTLS; secrets in Vault; CDE segment; least-privilege IAM
scores.rationale: The per-phase table gives concrete security controls in every phase from 0 to 6.

scores.evidence: The auth host's trace ID is propagated through OpenTelemetry across every tier. Prometheus metrics ... An alert fires when timeouts exceed 1% over 5 min.
scores.rationale: Phase 0 has observability, and every later phase has specific signals.

scores.evidence: Terraform, image digests, signed artifacts, everything through CI/CD
scores.rationale: Every phase has concrete reproducibility measures, such as snapshots, pinned seeds and versioned config.

scores.evidence: 80 ms hard timeout; flag off; rollback rehearsed
scores.rationale: Each phase has specific failure handling, including fallback, breaker, idempotent backfill, state rebuild and no auto-promotion.

scores.evidence: 1. Guardrail defense ... Phase 1; 2. Cost + latency budget; 3. Human-in-the-loop gating ... 4. Retrieval ... 5. Model access ... 9. Feedback
scores.rationale: Defenses, budgets and human gating are built in Phase 1, and the later layers follow in order: retrieval, model, memory, orchestration, routing (deferred), feedback. Memory comes in Phase 3 alongside retrieval, which is a minor nit.

scores.evidence: Decommissioning the rules engine (this is the point of no return): pull forward when it is proposed after ≥ 2 quarters at 100% enforcement.
scores.rationale: Each deferred item comes with a concrete pull-forward condition.

note: This is a very strong plan. It has a real production walking skeleton, explicit gates and flip conditions, concerns threaded through every phase, and the AI layers in the right order. I found no significant gaps.
